properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued September 21 at 12:28AM MDT until September 21 at 1:15AM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
SVRBOU

The National Weather Service in Denver has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Southeastern Elbert County in east central Colorado...
Southern Lincoln County in east central Colorado...

* Until 115 AM MDT.

* At 1228 AM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 4 miles northwest
of Punkin Center, or 27 miles south of Limon, moving southeast at
25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and half dollar size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Punkin Center and Karval.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Tornadoes can develop quickly from severe thunderstorms. Seek shelter
immediately in an interior room on the lowest floor of a well-built
structure.

properties.areaDesc: Suwannee; Gilchrist; Eastern Hamilton; Western Hamilton; Western Alachua; Northern Columbia; Southeastern Columbia; Southwestern Columbia; Echols; Clinch
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 21 at 2:02AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
Surface observations and local webcams indicate that patchy to
areas of locally dense fog were developing across portions of the
Suwannee Valley in inland northeast Florida as well as portions of
inland southeast Georgia. Fog may expand and become dense across
inland locations to the west of the U.S. Highway 301 corridor
through the early morning hours on Monday.

The nature of the fog is such that visibilities will vary greatly
over short distances. Motorists should be alert for rapidly
changing conditions through sunrise. If driving, slow down and
leave extra distance ahead of you in case a sudden stop is needed.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 21 at 2:00AM AST until September 21 at 3:00PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...All of Puerto Rico, including Vieques and Culebra, and the
U.S. Virgin Islands.


* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 3 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 21 at 1:54AM EDT until September 21 at 5:00AM EDT by NWS Pittsburgh PA
properties.description:
FFWPBZ

The National Weather Service in Pittsburgh has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Muskingum County in east central Ohio...

* Until 500 AM EDT.

* At 154 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain
has fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Zanesville, South Zanesville, Philo, Fultonham, Cannelville, East
Fultonham, Duncan Falls and Blue Rock State Park.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.senderName: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 11:18PM MDT until September 23 at 7:00PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Much of south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas,
including El Paso, Las Cruces, and the Mesilla Valley.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Wednesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of arroyos,
rivers, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water
crossings may be flooded, resulting in road closures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An early season back door cold front will interact with a late
season plume of deep monsoonal moisture, bringing several rounds
of thunderstorms with torrential downpours to the region Tuesday
afternoon through Wednesday evening. Repeated thunderstorms may
tend to focus in one or two areas, resulting in higher end
precipitation totals. The most critical period with the heaviest
rain potential will likely be Tuesday night into Wednesday
morning.
- A broad swath of moderate to locally heavy rainfall is likely to
affect most of the Watch area between late Tuesday afternoon and
Wednesday evening, with typical, scattered monsoon season flood
impacts. However, there is increasing potential for a narrow band
of repeated thunderstorms which will result in particularly heavy
rainfall amounts, possibly exceeding 3 inches in a 6 to 12 hour
period, resulting in higher-end impacts. Forecast models
currently favor placing the focus for heaviest rainfall over the
Mesilla Valley and El Paso. But forecasts this far out,
especially when dealing with thunderstorms, are simply not
accurate enough to precisely tell yet where exactly this area of
heaviest rainfall will set up. It could just as easily shift west
or east and avoid the more populated corridor.
- http://www.weather.gov/ElPaso
properties.instruction:
The forecast will be fine-tuned and will evolve over time. You should
monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood Warnings
Tuesday afternoon and evening. The Wednesday morning commute may also
be impacted. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Wisconsin...Illinois...

Fox River Lower Near New Munster affecting Kenosha and Lake
Counties.

Root River Canal At Raymond affecting Racine County.

.Two rivers in southeast Wisconsin remain in flood stage following
recent rains of 3.5 to 4.5 inches.

* WHERE...Fox River Lower near New Munster.

* WHEN...Until late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Water is up to the first floor levels of
some homes in the Town of Wheatland, Silver Lake and Village of
Salem Lakes area along Riverside Drive and Shorewood Drive. Hoosier
Creek Rd floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 11.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 10.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 PM CDT Sunday was 11.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.9 feet
early tomorrow afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
late Wednesday evening.
- Flood stage is 11.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.7
feet on 05/10/2019.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

A Flood Watch means water levels above flood stage are possible, but
not yet certain, based upon the latest forecasts. Persons along
rivers and streams in the watch area should monitor the latest
forecasts and be prepared to take action should flooding develop.

These forecasts are based on observed precipitation as well as
forecast precipitation 24 hours into the future. Changes to the
rainfall forecast, or any additional rainfall after 24 hours, may
cause changes to these river forecasts.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by Monday afternoon.

properties.instruction:
A Flood Warning means flooding is imminent or may already be
occurring. Persons along rivers, creeks, and other waterways should
take immediate precautions to protect life and property.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Campers and hikers should be especially cautious during periods of
heavy rainfall and flooding. Know your location relative to rivers,
streams, or drainage areas. Heavy rainfall can cause quick rises on
waterways, including trails or campgrounds that are usually dry.

properties.areaDesc: Municipality of Skagway; Haines Borough and Klukwan
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 20 at 1:38PM AKDT until September 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A low pressure system will continue to affect the panhandle through
this weekend bringing prolonged rain combined with high freezing
levels to increase ice melt on glacier river systems. The heavy
rainfall and associated runoff will produce significant river rises
with the potential of minor flooding.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...The following area, Northern Inner Channels. This includes
the cities of Skagway and Haines.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, other low-lying areas and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of lows will bring a prolonged period of rain combined
with warmer temperatures aloft allowing for any precipitation
falling into the region to remain as rain. Showers will continue
to move through the area this afternoon and evening. Some of
these showers could be heavy at times

For the Skagway area, Up to an inch of rain is still possible
through this afternoon into the overnight hours tonight. The
Haines area could see anywhere from 0.5 to 1 inch of rain during
the same time period.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Persons living along streams should stay alert and be prepared to
take action if a warning or advisory is issued, or flooding is
observed.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 20 at 2:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
An active monsoon pattern has developed across Western Micronesia
with recent satellite imagery showing broad areas of heavy showers
and thunderstorms. Midday satellite-derived surface wind data depicts
15 to 20 mph west winds across Yap State with a few areas of stronger
gusts north of Faraulep.

Computer models point to a continuation of these conditions into
midweek with periods of heavy showers moving across the islands,
occasionally bringing increased winds, gusts and choppy seas. By
midweek, models indicate the potential for a circulation to slowly
organize as it passes between Yap and Guam into the Philippine Sea.
As this happens, westerly winds and gusts will increase with showers
and thunderstorms. While these conditions will generally be felt
across Yap State, portions of the Republic of Palau could see heavy
showers and thunderstorms dropping south early in the week.

Residents should continue to monitor forecasts and listen for any
marine advisories that may be issued over the next several days.
Be aware of the latest weather conditions and trends before traveling
between islands. Stay up-to-date with all the latest forecasts at
weather.gov/gum and by following the latest information from your
local Weather Service Office.

NWSheadline: HEAVY SHOWERS AND THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS YAP STATE THROUGH MIDWEEK... ...WEST WINDS TO BE GUSTY AT TIMES
